entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving and partner institutions contributing. UK groups have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies, the sensors that detect the electrical signals produced when neutrinos interact in liquid argon. Black Hills State University has also joined the collaboration as an institutional member.

entry.title: KM3NeT and gravitational waves
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The KM3NeT Collaboration presented a paper on searches for coincident gravitational waves and high-energy neutrinos, using data from KM3NeT and ANTARES during the O3 observing run. The motivation is that sources of gravitational waves may produce high-energy neutrinos. The collaboration also held its Autumn 2026 meeting in Siracusa, with status updates on detector operations on the agenda.

entry.title: Auger and sterile neutrinos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Pierre Auger Collaboration studied the sensitivity of the observatory to sterile neutrinos with masses from MeV to 100 MeV, in a minimal 3+1 framework with mixing mainly to the tau flavour. Such neutrinos could cross long chords of the Earth and produce tau leptons that decay in the atmosphere, generating detectable air showers. The paper computes the corresponding exposures with a Monte Carlo simulation.

entry.title: nEXO backgrounds
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A simulation study estimates the cosmogenic background rate for nEXO, a five-tonne liquid-xenon TPC for neutrinoless double beta decay, if it is placed at SNOLAB. It compares results from Geant4 and FLUKA simulations of muons reaching the underground site.

entry.title: Project 8 atom source
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Project 8 aims to measure the neutrino mass with cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy of tritium beta decay, with a stated goal of 40 meV/c^2 for its final measurement. A new paper describes a prototype electron cyclotron resonance dissociator that ignites a hydrogen plasma, as a step towards dissociating molecular tritium.

entry.title: CMS heavy neutral leptons
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CMS reported a search for a Majorana heavy neutral lepton produced in top quark decays, using 13 TeV proton-proton data corresponding to 138 fb^-1 collected in 2016-2018. The search targets final states with same-sign, same-flavour dileptons in the type-I seesaw framework.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, including uncertainties in cross sections and hadronic interactions.

entry.title: Using the updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the authors infer the conditions for neutri
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Using the updated IceCube data for NGC 1068 down to about 0.2 TeV, the authors infer the conditions for neutrino production near the supermassive black hole. They compute hadronic neutrino production and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, sampling the parameter space with Latin hypercube sampling. This bears on what physical conditions are required to explain the first extragalactic neutrino source.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is phase blind. A rate anisotropy in the decoherence can supply a phase reference. It defines when decoherence effects could in principle reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free d
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free dark photon models. They derive exclusion limits for six benchmark models and find that their stringency correlates with the leptonic charge assignments. This shows how dark matter detectors can also test new physics in the neutrino sector.

entry.title: The paper offers semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion i
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper offers semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in multienergy neutrino ensembles. It is aimed at supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics. The authors report excellent agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering.
